'''Jon Leuer''' (born May 14, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 40th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. During his [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) career, he also played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Phoenix Suns]], and [[Detroit Pistons]].

==High school career==
Leuer was born in [[Long Lake, Minnesota]] and attended [[Orono school district|Orono High School]] in Long Lake, where he was ranked the 82nd-best college recruit in the nation from the class of 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-1611 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals.com Rivals150 2007 |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=June 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100630070900/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-1611 |url-status=live }}</ref> One scouting report read: "At 6-foot-10, 228-pounds, Leuer definitely needs some time to fill out his frame for high-major competition. Nonetheless, he is a pure shooter with good overall skills with the ball. He can knock down a jump hook and can play off the dribble. He moves well up and down the court, but has a ways to go defensively and as a rebounder. Could be an impact player with his size and unique skill set if he does get stronger."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jon-Leuer-52068;_ylt=Ajd.cPsdVI8RuNM32I6SwiLVO5B4 |title=Jon Leuer – Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |access-date=2013-10-17}}</ref>

Another one stated: "Flew under the radar prior to the spring of 2006. Excellent player from behind the stripe, especially when you consider that he pushes 6-10. Face up four man will need to add strength to reach his potential. Could be an [[Andrew Brackman]] type of forward."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1985852 |title=Scout.com: Jon Leuer Profile |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=March 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308112819/http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1985852 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his [[junior year]], he averaged 18 points and 8 [[rebounds]] per game and earned honorable mention all-state and first-team all-conference honors. He averaged 23.2 points and 12.0 rebounds per game as a senior and was selected to [[Minnesota]] State [[All-star game]] while landing second-team all-state and first-team all-conference honors. He ended up with 35 double digit scoring games and a career high of 37.<ref name="college_bio">[http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html Jon Leuer Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101026071854/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leuer_jon00.html |date=2010-10-26 }}</ref>

He played [[AAU basketball]] with the Minnesota Magic.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.magicbasketball.org/magic_alumni.htm |title=Minnesota MAGIC Basketball |publisher=Magicbasketball.org |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=2013-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017192214/http://www.magicbasketball.org/magic_alumni.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Leuer had originally entered high school as a [[Guard (basketball)|guard]], but had a 10-inch [[growth spurt]] before his [[senior (education)|senior year]].<ref name="college_bio" />

==College career==

=== Freshman season (2007–2008) ===
Leuer never started, but played in 32 games during the 2007–2008 season for the Wisconsin Badgers. The most points he scored during the non-conference season was 12, but he exploded for 25 (on 8 of 9 shooting) against the [[Michigan Wolverines]] in the [[Big Ten]] opener. However, after scoring 7 in the follow-up game, Leuer would only score 9 points for the remainder of the season. Much of this spoke to Wisconsin's great depth, as the Badgers would go on to win both the [[Big Ten]] regular season, with a 16–2 record, and [[Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten Conference tournament]]. They would later advance to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet Sixteen]] in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] and finished with a 31–5 record.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2007-08-sched.html|title=The Official Athletic Site of the Wisconsin Badgers – Men's Basketball|publisher=UWBadgers.com|access-date=2013-10-17|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130414060104/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2007-08-sched.html|archive-date=2013-04-14}}</ref> Leuer finished the season averaging 2.9 points per game and 1.3 rebounds in 8.6 minutes.

=== Sophomore season (2008–2009) ===
Leuer played in all 33 games and started the final 12 games of the year during the 2008–2009 season. He had 13 double digit scoring games including 17 in a [[victory]] at [[Virginia Tech]] in the [[ACC-Big Ten Challenge]]. He had a season high of 19 points against [[SIU-Edwardsville]]. He averaged 8.8 points per game and 3.8 rebounds in 21.3 minutes. The Badgers finished tied for fourth in the [[Big Ten]] with a 10–8 record, and a 20–13 record overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36138&year=2009 |title=NCAA College Basketball Players – NCAA Basketball – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=2013-10-17}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> They would upset the #5 seeded [[Florida State Seminoles]] in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] before succumbing to the [[Xavier Musketeers]] in the second round.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2008-09-sched.html|title=The Official Athletic Site of the Wisconsin Badgers – Men's Basketball|publisher=UWBadgers.com|access-date=2013-10-17|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130414072325/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-2008-09-sched.html|archive-date=2013-04-14}}</ref> Leuer was named to the Academic All-Big Ten Team.<ref name="college_bio" />

=== Junior season (2009–2010) ===
The Badgers went into the 2009–2010 season picked 9th in the [[Big Ten]]. However, they upset the [[Arizona Wildcats]] and [[Maryland Terrapins]] in the [[Maui Invitational]].<ref>[http://www.mauiinvitational.com/index.asp#]   {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100929232609/http://www.mauiinvitational.com/index.asp |date=September 29, 2010 }}</ref> On December 2, 2009, in a game on [[ESPN]], Wisconsin shocked the #5 [[Duke Blue Devils]] (who would be the eventual National Champions).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://badgerherald.com/news/2009/12/03/badgers_shock_duke_a.php |title=The Badger Herald: News: Badgers shock Duke at Kohl Center |publisher=Archive.is |access-date=2013-10-17 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121124134039/http://badgerherald.com/news/2009/12/03/badgers_shock_duke_a.php |archive-date=2012-11-24 }}</ref> Leuer poured in 17 points on his way to scoring double digits in 13 of the first 15 games of the year. He followed up the effort against Duke with back-to-back double doubles at [[UW-Green Bay]] (a career high 26 points and 10 rebounds) and against [[Marquette University]] (24 points, 12 rebounds). He would also score 25 against [[UW-Milwaukee]] and 21 at [[Michigan State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=36138&year=2010 |title=NCAA College Basketball Players – NCAA Basketball – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=2013-10-17}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Wisconsin was off to a surprising 13–3 start (3–1 in the [[Big Ten]]) after a 73–66 upset against #4 [[Purdue]]. However, Leuer had an off night against [[Purdue]] and only scored 4 points on 2-15 shooting. It was revealed after the game that Leuer had broken his [[wrist]] in the first half, yet still played 38 of the 40 minutes in the game. Leuer was ruled out indefinitely and he ended up missing the next 9 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Badgers lose Leuer with broken wrist| date=11 January 2010 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4816123|publisher=[[ESPN]] | access-date=30 October 2010}}</ref>

When Leuer returned, he was eased back into the lineup, scoring 4 points in his first game back, a loss against the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. However, Leuer would score double digits in each of the final five games of the year, including 20 against the [[University of Illinois]], as the Badgers went 4–1 down the stretch and finished 13–5 in the [[Big Ten]], good enough for fourth place and a #13 national ranking. Leuer won [[Big Ten]] Player of the week for the final week of the regular season. Yet, the Badgers would lose to the [[Illinois Fighting Illini]] in the first round of the [[Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] and were upset by [[Cornell]] in the second round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]], despite 14 and 23 points from Leuer respectively.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-sched-2009.html |title=The Official Athletic Site of the Wisconsin Badgers – Men's Basketball |publisher=UWBadgers.com |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130414051754/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/archive/wis-m-baskbl-sched-2009.html |archive-date=2013-04-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Leuer ended up leading the Badgers in points per game (15.4), rebounds per game (5.8), and blocks per game (1.33). Due to the wrist injury, he only played in 24 games, starting 22 of them. His .522 [[field-goal percentage]] was the highest by a Wisconsin player since [[Alando Tucker]]'s .533 mark in 2003. He earned honorable mention All-[[Big Ten]], despite missing half of the conference games. He also made the Academic All-[[Big Ten]] team for the second straight year.<ref name="college_bio" />

During the summer, Leuer was selected to be on the United States men's select team, a team of [[college]] players hand-picked to help the [[United States men's national basketball team]] prepare for the [[FIBA World Championships]]. Leuer went with the team to [[New York City]] to compete against the likes of [[Kobe Bryant]], [[LeBron James]], and [[Dwyane Wade]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_86cc4150-8aaa-11df-9820-001cc4c03286.html |title=UW men's basketball: Leuer to train with U.S. national team : Sports |publisher=Host.madison.com |date=2010-07-08 |access-date=2013-10-17}}</ref> Leuer had been named to the team after impressing [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]], and [[Villanova Wildcats|Villanova]], [[coach (sport)|coach]], [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]]. When Gary Parrish of [[CBSSports.com]] asked Wright to name the best [[college]] player with the [[USA Basketball]] select team, Wright picked Leuer over [[Kyle Singler]], [[Nolan Smith]], [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]] and others.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_29ed892c-9a49-11df-b22a-001cc4c03286.html |title=UW men's basketball: Leuer draws praise after cameo with USA Basketball : Sports |publisher=Host.madison.com |date=2010-07-28 |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=July 31, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100731070539/http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_29ed892c-9a49-11df-b22a-001cc4c03286.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

"He's really good," Wright told Parrish. "Maybe I haven't followed him as well because he's from the [[Midwest]], and maybe he wouldn't surprise anybody else. But he's got great size, he puts it on the floor, he passes it, he can shoot it. He's just a ballplayer." When asked if he would be an [[NBA]] player, Wright answered "yes."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_5754bc22-9e5f-11df-9ada-001cc4c002e0.html |title=UW men's basketball: Leuer lands another stint with USA Basketball : Sports |publisher=Host.madison.com |date=2010-08-02 |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=August 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805134054/http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/article_5754bc22-9e5f-11df-9ada-001cc4c002e0.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Senior season (2010–2011) ===
[[SI.com]] named Leuer their Big Ten preseason player of the year. About Leuer, Luke Winn wrote, "Watch out for Leuer, an ultra-efficient, 6-foot-10 forward who'll be the Badgers' clear No. 1 offensive option for the first time in his career."

On December 28, 2010, the Badgers upset then #13 ranked [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]], 68–60. During the first half of the game, Leuer became the 36th player in Wisconsin Badgers history to score 1,000 points in a career.

On March 1, 2011, Leuer was named to the [[Yahoo Sports]] All-Big Ten 1st team.<ref>{{cite web|last=King |first=Jason |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news;_ylt=AiMYsNUhdGD6.szznqPvLwbevbYF?slug=jn-bigten030111 |title=Yahoo! Sports' All-Big Ten Team – Yahoo Sports |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date=2011-03-01 |access-date=2013-10-17}}</ref>

He was picked to the Third Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media |date=Mar 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }}</ref> Leuer was named to the [[Yahoo Sports]] All-American Team Honorable Mention.<ref>{{cite web |last=King |first=Jason |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=jn-allam030711 |title=Yahoo! Sports' All-American Team – Yahoo Sports |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date=2011-03-07 |access-date=2013-10-17 |archive-date=March 9, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309223922/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=jn-allam030711 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Skyliners Frankfurt (2011)===
On June 23, 2011, Leuer was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 40th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/prospects/jon-leuer/ |title=Prospect Profile: Jon Leuer |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109002934/http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/prospects/jon-leuer/ |archive-date=January 9, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He had a stint in Germany with [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] during the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/6836375/milwaukee-bucks-draft-pick-jon-leuer-signs-play-germany |title=Jon Leuer signs with Skyliners Frankfurt |work=ESPN.com |date=August 5, 2011 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=August 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829072733/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/6836375/milwaukee-bucks-draft-pick-jon-leuer-signs-play-germany |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Milwaukee Bucks (2011–2012) ===
Leuer joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]] in December 2011.

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2012–2013)===
On June 27, 2012, Leuer was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] along with [[Jon Brockman]], [[Shaun Livingston]], and the 12th pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] in exchange for [[Samuel Dalembert]] and the 14th pick in the 2012 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8104029/source-houston-rockets-make-trade-milwaukee-bucks-move-12 |title=Rockets trade for No. 12 pick |work=ESPN.com |date=June 28, 2012 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=July 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728120017/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8104029/source-houston-rockets-make-trade-milwaukee-bucks-move-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was waived by the Rockets on July 18.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10560 |title=Rockets waive Jon Leuer and Jerome Jordan |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 18, 2012 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112135427/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10560 |archive-date=November 12, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 20, 2012, Leuer was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/leuer_120720.html |title=Cavaliers Claim Jon Leuer Off Waivers from Houston |work=NBA.com |date=July 20, 2012 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=May 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200531090235/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/leuer_120720.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 7, he was sent down to the Cavaliers' D-League affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/cavaliers_assign_leuer__char_2012_12_07.html |title=Cavaliers Assign Leuer to Charge |work=NBA.com |date=December 7, 2012 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |url-status=dead on December 20,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-leuer-121220 |title=Cavaliers Recall Jon Leuer |work=NBA.com |date=December 20, 2012 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=October 26, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026215526/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-leuer-121220 |url-status=live }}</ref> reassigned on January 3, 2013,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/charge_reassign_leuer_2013_01_03.html |title=Cleveland Cavaliers Re-Assign Jon Leuer to NBA D-League Affiliate Canton Charge |work=NBA.com |archive-date=October 26, 2013 }}</ref> and recalled again on January 7.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/recall-leuer-130107 |title=Cavaliers Recall Jon Leuer |work=NBA.com |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2015)===
[[file:Jon Leuer March 2013.jpg|thumb|Leuer in March 2013]]
On January 22, 2013, Leuer was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Marreese Speights]], [[Wayne Ellington]], [[Josh Selby]], and a future first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade-130122 |title=Cavaliers Acquire Speights, Ellington, Selby and Future First Round Pick From Grizzlies |work=NBA.com |date=January 22, 2013 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=February 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207182233/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade-130122 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On July 15, 2013, Leuer was re-signed by the Grizzlies to a three-year, $3 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13774 |title=Memphis Grizzlies re-sign Jon Leuer |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 15, 2013 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728224921/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13774 |archive-date=July 28, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/228582/Jon-Leuer-To-Sign-Three-Year-$3M-Deal-With-Grizzlies |title=Jon Leuer To Sign Three-Year, $3M Deal With Grizzlies |work=RealGM.com |date=July 3, 2013 |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-date=September 8, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130908004407/http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/228582/Jon-Leuer-To-Sign-Three-Year-$3M-Deal-With-Grizzlies |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 3, Leuer recorded a career-high 23 points, along with nine rebounds and three blocks, in a 110–91 win over the [[2013–14 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]]. Six days later, he recorded his first career double-double with 16 points and a career-high 12 rebounds in a 94–85 win over the [[2013–14 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]]. Leuer tied his career–high of 23 points on January 5, 2014, in a 112–84 win over the [[2013–14 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leuerjo01/gamelog/2014/ |title=Jon Leuer 2013–14 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 12, 2014 |archive-date=November 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112130902/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leuerjo01/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On December 7, 2014, Leuer had a season-best game with 20 points and career-high tying 12 rebounds in a 103–87 win over the [[2014–15 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].<ref>[http://miami.cbslocal.com/2014/12/07/leuers-double-double-leads-grizzlies-past-heat/ Leuer’s Double-Double Leads Grizzlies Past Heat]</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2015–2016)===
On June 25, 2015, Leuer was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-aquire-jon-leuer-memphis|title=Suns Acquire Jon Leuer From Memphis|date=June 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015|archive-date=June 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628193221/http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-aquire-jon-leuer-memphis|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns in the team's season opener against the [[2015–16 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] on October 28, recording 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench in a 111–95 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=8 Dallas players reach double figures, Mavs rout Suns 111-95|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330130800/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 12, he recorded his first double-double as a Sun, recording 10 points and 11 rebounds in a 118–104 win over the [[2015–16 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Knight, Bledsoe lead Suns past short-handed Clippers 118-104|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2015|access-date=November 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161103201740/http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Two days later, he received his first starting assignment for the Suns, recording seven points and five rebounds in just under 19 minutes of action, helping the Suns defeat the [[2015–16 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]] 105–81.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/DENPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Bledsoe leads Suns over cold-shooting Nuggets, 105-81|work=NBA.com|date=November 14, 2015|access-date=November 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151116172902/http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/DENPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 16, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 25, Leuer had a then season-best game with 20 points and 12 rebounds in a loss to the [[2015–16 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151125/NOPPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Anthony Davis lead Pelicans past Suns, 120-114|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2015|access-date=November 25, 2015|archive-date=November 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151122062021/http://www.nba.com/games/20151125/NOPPHX/gameinfo.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 21, 2016, Leuer recorded his seventh double-double of the season (ninth of his career)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/712126065787871232|title=@JLeu30 has his seventh double-double of the...|work=Twitter|date=March 21, 2016|access-date=March 24, 2016}}</ref> with 13 points and 13 rebounds in a loss to his former team, the [[2015–16 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]]. Two days later, he had 22 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in a 119–107 win over the [[2015–16 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160323/LALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Bryant scores 17 in Phoenix finale but Lakers lose again|work=NBA.com|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=March 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326081840/http://www.nba.com/games/20160323/LALPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 26, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> recording back-to-back double-doubles for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/712852722161213440|title=@JLeu30 now has back-to-back double-...|work=Twitter|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=March 24, 2016}}</ref> In the Suns' season finale on April 13, Leuer recorded 16 points and matched his career best with 14 rebounds in a 114–105 win over the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Teletovic's 22 leads Suns past Clippers reserves, 114-105|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2016|access-date=April 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417140820/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2016–2019)===
On July 8, 2016, Leuer signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-ish-smith-and-jon-leuer|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agents Ish Smith and Jon Leuer|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016|archive-date=July 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160711144033/http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-ish-smith-and-jon-leuer|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 30, he scored a then season-high 22 points in a 105–98 loss to the [[2016–17 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899940|title=Korver, Howard lead Hawks past Pistons, 105-98|work=ESPN.com|date=December 30, 2016|access-date=December 31, 2016|archive-date=December 31, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231170619/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899940|url-status=live}}</ref> On February 3, 2017, Leuer scored a career-high 24 points in a 116–108 win over the [[2016–17 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900153|title=Morris, Leuer lead Pistons over Timberwolves 116-108|work=ESPN.com|date=February 3, 2017|access-date=February 3, 2017|archive-date=February 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170205095702/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900153|url-status=live}}</ref>

Leuer played in only eight games during the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]] due to an ankle injury, and he decided to have season-ending surgery on it in January.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975415|title=Wizards score 45 in 3rd, beat Pistons 122-112|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2018|access-date=January 19, 2018|archive-date=January 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120124627/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975415|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2018, he was reported to have taken surgery on his right knee to repair his medial meniscus.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/08/09/pistons-jon-leuer-right-knee-operation|title=Detroit Pistons' Jon Leuer undergoes right knee operation|work=NBA.com|date=August 9, 2018|access-date=August 9, 2018|archive-date=August 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810120809/http://www.nba.com/article/2018/08/09/pistons-jon-leuer-right-knee-operation|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 27, 2018, in a 109–89 loss to the [[2018–19 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]], Leuer made his [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]] debut, his first appearance since October 31, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070755|title=Celtics hand Pistons first loss of season, 109-89|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2018|access-date=October 27, 2018|archive-date=October 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181028073918/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070755|url-status=live}}</ref>

On June 20, 2019, Leuer was traded back to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]] and the draft rights to [[Kevin Porter Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-aquire-jon-leuer-detroit|title=Bucks Acquire Jon Leuer From Detroit|work=NBA.com|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 20, 2019|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030141752/https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-aquire-jon-leuer-detroit|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 9, Leuer was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jon-leuer-waived-by-bucks/|title=Jon Leuer: Waived by Bucks|work=cbssports.com|date=July 9, 2019|access-date=July 9, 2019}}</ref>

Leuer announced his retirement over [[Instagram]] on May 24, 2020, at the age of 31.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Jake|last1=Kocorowski|url=https://www.si.com/college/wisconsin/basketball/jon-leuer-retires-detroit-pistons-milwaukee-bucks-wisconsin-basketball|title=Former Wisconsin Forward Jon Leuer Announces Retirement|date=May 24, 2020|website=si.com|access-date=May 24, 2020|archive-date=June 5, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605223352/https://www.si.com/college/wisconsin/basketball/jon-leuer-retires-detroit-pistons-milwaukee-bucks-wisconsin-basketball|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Leuer is the son of Mike and Holly Leuer, has two older sisters, Maren and Katie, and is married to Keegan Billick, the daughter of longtime [[Baltimore Ravens]] head coach [[Brian Billick]]. He was [[majoring]] in [[history]] while at the [[University of Wisconsin]].<ref name="college_bio" />
